      <content name="title">&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;Muscle&lt;/span&gt; Disorders</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Myopathies</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Rhabdomyolysis</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Myopathy</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">&lt;p&gt;Your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; help you move and help your body work. Different types of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; have different jobs. There are many problems that can affect &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles. Muscle&lt;/span&gt; disorders can &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; weakness, pain or even paralysis. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;Causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; disorders include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Injury or overuse, such as sprains or strains, &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; or tendinitis &lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;A genetic disorder, such as &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscular&lt;/span&gt; dystrophy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Some cancers&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Inflammation, such as myositis&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Diseases of nerves that affect &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Infections&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sometimes the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; disorders is unknown.&lt;/p&gt;</content>
      <content name="mesh">&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;Muscular&lt;/span&gt; Diseases</content>
      <content name="groupName">Bones, Joints and &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;Muscles&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="snippet"> ... Diseases of nerves that affect &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;  Infections  Certain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;  Sometimes the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; disorders is unknown.</content>

    <document rank="1" url="https://medlineplus.gov/musclecramps.html">
      <content name="title">&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Charley Horse</content>
      <content name="altTitle">&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are sudden, involuntary contractions or spasms in one or more of your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;. They are very common and often occur after exercise. Some people get &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, especially leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, at night. They can be painful, and they may last a few seconds to several minutes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;You can have a &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramp&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; in any &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;, but they happen most often in the:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Thighs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Feet&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Hands&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Arms&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Abdomen&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Area along your ribcage&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;Causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Straining or overusing a &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;. This is the most common &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Compression of your nerves, from problems such as a spinal cord injury or a pinched nerve in the neck or back&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Dehydration&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Low levels of electrolytes such as magnesium, potassium, or calcium&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Not enough blood getting to your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnancy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting dialysis&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sometimes the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is unknown.&lt;/p&gt;Who is at risk for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;Anyone can get &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but they are more common in some people:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Older adults&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People who are overweight&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Athletes&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnant women&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;People with certain medical conditions, such as thyroid and nerve disorders&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;When do I need to see a health care provider for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;Muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; are usually harmless, and they go away after a few minutes. But you should contact your health care provider if the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are severe&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Happen frequently&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Don't get better with stretching and drinking enough fluids&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Last a long time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by swelling, redness, or a feeling of warmth&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Are accompanied by &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; weakness&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are the treatments for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;?&lt;p&gt;You usually don't need treatment for &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. You may be able to find some relief from &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; by:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretching or gently massaging the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Applying heat when the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; is tight and ice when the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscle&lt;/span&gt; is sore&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting more fluids if you are dehydrated&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;If another medical problem is causing the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, treating that problem will likely help. There are &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; that providers sometimes prescribe to prevent &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, but they are not always effective and may &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; side effects. Talk to your provider about the risks and benefits of &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;Can &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; be prevented?&lt;p&gt;To prevent &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;muscle &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;&lt;span class="qt6"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, you can:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stretch your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;, especially before exercising. If you often get leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; at night, stretch your leg &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; before bed.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Drink plenty of liquids. If you do intense exercise or exercise in the heat, sports drinks can help you replace electrolytes.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>

    <document rank="2" url="https://medlineplus.gov/periodpain.html">
      <content name="title">Period Pain</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Dysmenorrhea</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Menstrual &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Menstrual pain</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are painful periods?&lt;p&gt;Menstruation, or period, is normal vaginal bleeding that happens as part of a woman's monthly cycle. Many women have painful periods, also called dysmenorrhea. The pain is most often menstrual &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;, which are a throbbing, cramping pain in your lower abdomen. You may also have other symptoms, such as lower back pain, nausea, diarrhea, and headaches. Period pain is not the same as premenstrual syndrome (PMS). PMS &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; many different symptoms, including weight gain, bloating, irritability, and fatigue. PMS often starts one to two weeks before your period starts.&lt;/p&gt;What &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; painful periods?&lt;p&gt;There are two types of dysmenorrhea: primary and secondary. Each type has different &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Primary dysmenorrhea is the most common kind of period pain. It is period pain that is not caused by another condition. The &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is usually having too many prostaglandins, which are chemicals that your uterus makes. These chemicals make the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; of your uterus tighten and relax, and this &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The pain can start a day or two before your period. It normally lasts for a few days, though in some women it can last longer.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;You usually first start having period pain when you are younger, just after you begin getting periods. Often, as you get older, you have less pain. The pain may also get better after you have given birth.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Secondary dysmenorrhea often starts later in life. It is caused by conditions that affect your uterus or other reproductive organs, such as endometriosis and uterine fibroids. This kind of pain often gets worse over time. It may begin before your period starts and continue after your period ends.&lt;/p&gt;What can I do about period pain?&lt;p&gt;To help ease your period pain, you can try:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Using a heating pad or hot water bottle on your lower abdomen&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Getting some exercise&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Taking a hot bath&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Doing relaxation techniques, including yoga and meditation&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;You might also try taking over-the-counter pain relievers such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). NSAIDs include ibuprofen and naproxen. Besides relieving pain, NSAIDs reduce the amount of prostaglandins that your uterus makes and lessen their effects.  This helps to lessen the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. You can take NSAIDs when you first have symptoms, or when your period starts. You can keep taking them for a few days. You should not take NSAIDS if you have ulcers or other stomach problems, bleeding problems, or liver disease. You should also not take them if you are allergic to aspirin. Always check with your health care provider if you are not sure whether or not you should take NSAIDs.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;It may also help to get enough rest and avoid using alcohol and tobacco.&lt;/p&gt;When should I get medical help for my period pain?&lt;p&gt;For many women, some pain during your period is normal. However, you should contact your health care provider if:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;NSAIDs and self-care measures don't help, and the pain interferes with your life&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; suddenly get worse&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;You are over 25 and you get severe &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; for the first time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;You have a fever with your period pain&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;You have the pain even when you are not getting your period&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;How is the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of severe period pain diagnosed?&lt;p&gt;To diagnose severe period pain, your health care provider will ask you about your medical history and do a pelvic exam. You may also have an ultrasound or other imaging test. If your health care provider thinks you have secondary dysmenorrhea, you might have laparoscopy. It is a surgery that lets your health care provider look inside your body.&lt;/p&gt;What are treatments for severe period pain?&lt;p&gt;If your period pain is primary dysmenorrhea and you need medical treatment, your health care provider might suggest using hormonal birth control, such as the pill, patch, ring, or IUD. Another treatment option might be prescription pain relievers.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;If you have secondary dysmenorrhea, your treatment depends upon the condition that is causing the problem. In some cases, you may need surgery.&lt;/p&gt;</content>

      <content name="groupName">Women</content>
      <content name="groupName">Female Reproductive System</content>
      <content name="snippet"> ... usually having too many prostaglandins, which are chemicals that your uterus makes. These chemicals make the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; of your uterus tighten and relax, and this &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; the &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. The pain can start a day or two  ... </content>

    <document rank="3" url="https://medlineplus.gov/peripheralnervedisorders.html">
      <content name="title">Peripheral Nerve Disorders</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Neuropathy</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Neuritis</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Peripheral neuritis</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Peripheral neuropathy</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are peripheral nerves?&lt;p&gt;Nerves are like wires that carry messages back and forth between your brain and your body. Your peripheral nerves branch off from your brain and spinal cord and connect to all parts of your body, including your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; and organs. Peripheral nerves carry messages from your brain that control your movement, breathing, heartbeat, digestion, and more. They also carry messages from your body to your brain, so you can feel things, such as pain, heat, and cold.&lt;/p&gt;What are peripheral nerve disorders?&lt;p&gt;Peripheral nerve disorders happen when one or more peripheral nerves are damaged. Damaged nerves may not carry messages correctly, or they may not work at all. As a result, you may have pain, trouble walking, or a variety of other problems, depending on which nerves are involved.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Peripheral nerve disorders are very common. There are more than 100 different types.&lt;/p&gt;What &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; peripheral nerve disorders?&lt;p&gt;Many things can damage nerves and lead to peripheral nerve disorders:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Diabetes is the most common &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of peripheral nerve disorders. Most people with diabetes will develop diabetic nerve problems.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Physical injury (trauma) that stretches, crushes, squeezes, cuts, or puts pressure on one or more nerves. Some examples of peripheral nerve disorders from physical injury include  complex regional pain syndrome and brachial plexus injuries.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Health conditions, including:
	&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain cancers and their treatment (chemotherapy and radiation therapy).&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Infections, such as HIV and Lyme disease.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Problems with blood or blood vessels.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Kidney or liver disease.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Certain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Contact with certain toxic substances, such as lead or mercury.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Alcohol use disorder (AUD) and smoking.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Vitamin imbalances, especially a lack of vitamin B12.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Your genes, including changes in your genes or conditions that you inherit from your parents, such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;In certain cases, the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of peripheral nerve disorder is not known.&lt;/p&gt;What are the symptoms of peripheral nerve disorders?&lt;p&gt;The symptoms of peripheral nerve disorders depend on which nerves are affected, what is causing the damage, and how serious it is:&lt;/p&gt;Types of nervesPossible symptoms of nerve damageMotor nerves control your &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt; and all your movement, such as walking, talking, and using your hands.&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Weak or aching &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Problems with balance, walking, or using your arms and hands&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;Cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; or twitching &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;span class="qt4"&gt;Muscle&lt;/span&gt; shrinking&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;Sensory nerves carry messages to your brain from your senses, including touch, hot and cold, and pain.&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Tingling, numbness, or pain often in the hands and feet&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Not being able to feel heat, cold, or pain, such as a cut on your foot&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pain from even light touch&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;Autonomic nerves send messages to your organs to control breathing, digestion, and other body functions that happen without thinking about them.&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;A heartbeat that's too fast or too slow&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Trouble swallowing&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Sweating too much or too little&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Problems with urination or sexual function&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Symptoms may range from mild to very strong. They may develop quickly over days or slowly over months and years. But they are rarely life-threatening.&lt;/p&gt;How are peripheral nerve disorders diagnosed?&lt;p&gt;To find out if you have a peripheral nerve disorder, your provider will:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Ask about your medical history&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Ask about your family health history&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Do a physical exam&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Order tests, which may include:
	&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Blood tests&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Genetic tests&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Nerve tests that measure:
			&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Electrical activity in your nerves and &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;How well your autonomic nerves are working&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;
		&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;A biopsy of nerve or skin tissue&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;CT or MRI scan to see what may be pressing on your nerves&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are the treatments for peripheral nerve disorders?&lt;p&gt;It's important to treat any conditions that are causing nerve damage. In certain cases, that will allow your nerves to heal over time.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Treatment for symptoms depends on the type of peripheral nerve disorder you have, where it is, and how severe. Treatment options include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Braces or splints&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Over-the-counter patches and skin creams&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Prescription &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Non-drug pain management, such as electrical stimulation or relaxation therapy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Surgery to relieve pressure on a nerve&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;Can peripheral nerve disorders be prevented?&lt;p&gt;You can help prevent peripheral nerve disorders by:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Managing health conditions that may &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; nerve damage, especially diabetes&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Preventing falls and accidents&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Avoiding toxic substances&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Being careful to avoid repeated motions and body positions that press on your nerves&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Eating a balanced diet, exercising, limiting alcohol, and not smoking&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke&lt;/p&gt;</content>

    <document rank="4" url="https://medlineplus.gov/vasculardiseases.html">
      <content name="title">Vascular Diseases</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Cardiovascular Diseases</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Circulatory Disorders</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Hemangioma</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Veins</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are vascular diseases?&lt;p&gt;Your vascular system is your body's network of blood vessels. It includes your:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Arteries, which carry oxygen-rich blood from your heart to your tissues and organs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Veins, which carry the blood and waste products back to your heart&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Capillaries, which are tiny blood vessels that connect your small arteries to your small veins. The walls of the capillaries are thin and leaky, to allow for an exchange of materials between your tissues and blood.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Vascular diseases are conditions which affect your vascular system. They are common and can be serious. Some types include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Aneurysm - a bulge or "ballooning" in the wall of an artery&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Atherosclerosis - a disease in which plaque builds up inside your arteries. Plaque is made up of fat, cholesterol, calcium, and other substances found in the blood.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Blood clots, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Coronary artery disease and carotid artery disease, diseases that involve the narrowing or blockage of an artery. The &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is usually a buildup of plaque.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Raynaud phenomenon - a disorder that &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; the blood vessels to narrow when you are cold or feeling stressed&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Stroke - a serious condition that happens when blood flow to your brain stops.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Varicose veins - swollen, twisted veins that you can see just under the skin&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Vasculitis - inflammation of the blood vessels&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; vascular diseases?&lt;p&gt;The &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; of vascular diseases depend on the specific disease. These &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;causes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Genetics&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Heart diseases such as high cholesterol and high blood pressure&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Infection&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Injury&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;span class="qt0"&gt;Medicines&lt;/span&gt;, including hormones&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;p&gt;Sometimes the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; is unknown.&lt;/p&gt;Who is at risk for vascular diseases?&lt;p&gt;The risk factors for vascular diseases can vary, depending on the specific disease. But some of the more common risk factors include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Age - your risk of some diseases goes up as you get older&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Conditions that can affect the heart and blood vessels, such as diabetes or high cholesterol&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Family history of vascular or heart diseases&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Infection or injury that damages your veins&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Lack of exercise&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Obesity&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Pregnancy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Sitting or standing still for long periods of time&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Smoking&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are the symptoms of vascular diseases?&lt;p&gt;The symptoms for each disease are different.&lt;/p&gt;How are vascular diseases diagnosed?&lt;p&gt;To make a diagnosis, your health care provider will do a physical exam and ask about your symptoms and medical history. You may have imaging tests and/or blood tests.&lt;/p&gt;How are vascular diseases treated?&lt;p&gt;Which treatment you get depends on which vascular disease you have and how severe it is. Types of treatments for vascular diseases include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Lifestyle changes, such as eating a heart-healthy diet and getting more exercise&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;span class="qt0"&gt;Medicines&lt;/span&gt;, such as blood pressure &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;, blood thinners, cholesterol &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;, and clot-dissolving drugs. In some cases, providers use a catheter to send &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicine&lt;/span&gt; directly to a blood vessel.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Non-surgical procedures, such as angioplasty, stenting, and vein ablation&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Surgery&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;Can vascular diseases be prevented?&lt;p&gt;There are steps you can take to help prevent vascular diseases:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Make healthy lifestyle changes, such as eating a heart-healthy diet and getting more exercise&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Don't smoke. If you are already a smoker, talk to your health care provider for help in finding the best way for you to quit.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Keep your blood pressure and cholesterol in check&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;If you have diabetes, control your blood sugar&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Try not to sit or stand for up long periods of time. If you do need to sit all day, get up and move around every hour or so. If you are traveling on a long trip, you can also wear compression stockings and regularly stretch your legs.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>

    <document rank="5" url="https://medlineplus.gov/painrelievers.html">
      <content name="title">Pain Relievers</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Analgesics</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Narcotics</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Painkillers</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Pain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are pain relievers?&lt;p&gt;Pain relievers are &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; that reduce or relieve headaches, sore &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;muscles&lt;/span&gt;, arthritis, or other aches and pains.  There are many different pain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;, and each has advantages and risks. Some types of pain respond better to certain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; than others. Each person may also have a slightly different response to a pain reliever.&lt;/p&gt;What are the types of over-the-counter pain relievers?&lt;p&gt;Over-the-counter (OTC) &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; are good for many types of pain. Two types of OTC pain &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; are usually recommended for mild to moderate pain.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is used in many OTC and prescription &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt;. It's often considered safer than other pain relievers. Unfortunately, it's common for people to take too much accidentally. Be careful not to take too much each day or use more than one &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicine&lt;/span&gt; with acetaminophen. Check with your health care provider before taking &lt;span class="qt0"&gt;medicines&lt;/span&gt; containing acetaminophen for more than ten days or five days for your child.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) include aspirin, naproxen (Aleve), and ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin). These pain relievers are often most effective if you have pain and inflammation (swelling), such as for arthritis or menstrual &lt;span class="qt4"&gt;&lt;span class="qt5"&gt;cramps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;. If you take more than the recommended amount, NSAIDs may &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; nausea, stomach pain, or ulcers.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;What are prescription pain relievers?&lt;p&gt;If OTC pain relievers don't relieve your pain, your provider may prescribe something stronger. Many NSAIDs are also available at higher prescription doses.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;The most powerful pain relievers are opioids, sometimes called narcotics. They include strong prescription pain relievers such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, or morphine. Opioids are sometimes used to treat moderate to severe pain. Your provider may give you a prescription to reduce pain after you have had a major injury or surgery.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;Opioids are very effective, but they can sometimes have serious side effects. There is also a risk of addiction. Because of the risks, you must use them only under your provider's supervision.&lt;/p&gt;What are some non-drug treatments for pain?&lt;p&gt;Pain relievers are just one part of a pain treatment plan. Environmental factors, stress, and beliefs about pain may affect the way you feel about pain and respond to treatment.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;There are many things you can do to help ease pain. Treatment depends on the &lt;span class="qt2"&gt;&lt;span class="qt3"&gt;cause&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and type of pain. It's important to check with your provider before trying any of them. A few non-drug treatments for pain include:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Acupuncture&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Hot or cold packs&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Massage therapy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Physical therapy&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;Relaxation techniques&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;</content>
      <content name="mesh">Analgesics, Non-Narcotic</content>
      <content name="groupName">Drug Therapy</content>

It's important to check with your provider before trying any of them.
